findings.title: Administrative endpoint lacks role check
findings.description: A standard account can access an administrative endpoint.
findings.impact: Unauthorized administrative actions may be possible.
findings.replication_steps:
1. Sign in as a standard account.
2. Request the administrative endpoint.

findings.title: Verbose response header
findings.description: The application response discloses an implementation version in a response header.
findings.impact: The detail can help an attacker tailor reconnaissance and exploit research.
findings.mitigation: Remove unnecessary version headers from public responses.
findings.replication_steps:
1. Request the application home page.
2. Inspect returned response headers.

findings.title: Missing authorization on account export
findings.description: Changing an account identifier in an export request returns another account's data.
findings.impact: An unauthorized user could obtain data belonging to other accounts.
findings.mitigation: Enforce object-level authorization on every export request.
findings.replication_steps:
1. Sign in as a standard user.
2. Request an export for another account identifier.

findings.title: Password reset token is predictable
findings.description: The reset experience sends a short notification after a user requests assistance.
findings.impact: The service desk may receive duplicate requests during busy periods.
findings.mitigation: Review the workflow with the product team before the next release.
findings.replication_steps:
1. Request a password reset.
2. Observe the confirmation message.

findings.title: HTTP response metadata exposure
findings.description: The service reveals unnecessary metadata in an HTTP response.
findings.impact: The metadata can aid attacker reconnaissance.
findings.mitigation: Remove unnecessary metadata from public responses.
findings.references:
1. Request the endpoint.
2. Inspect the response headers.

findings.title: Session management permits fixation
findings.description: An attacker who fixes a known session identifier before login may access the authenticated session.
findings.impact: The application accepts a caller-controlled session identifier and does not rotate it after authentication.
findings.mitigation: Issue a new session identifier after authentication and reject caller-provided session identifiers.
findings.replication_steps:
1. Set a known session identifier.
2. Authenticate and observe that the identifier remains valid.
